account.accessRules.linkControl.en: Switch lights and sockets, and set the thermostat, on this dashboard
account.accessRules.linkControl.context: What a share link that can control can do.

account.accessRules.linkNoFlows.en: Start flows, open locks, set the alarm or open garage doors
account.accessRules.linkNoFlows.context: What a share link that can control still can’t do, since anyone with the link could. Flows are Homey’s automations.

account.accessRules.linkNoOthers.en: See your other dashboards, devices or account
account.accessRules.linkNoOthers.context: What a share link can’t do.

account.accessRules.linkSee.context: What a share link can do: watch the dashboard, updating live.

account.accessRules.noChange.context: What a view-only link or screen can’t do: tapping a tile does nothing.

account.accessRules.noLogin.en: Get your login or your Homey’s
account.accessRules.noLogin.context: What a share link or screen can’t do: it never gets the person’s login, nor their Homey’s.

account.accessRules.screenControl.en: Everything the panel’s tiles do, flows and locks included
account.accessRules.screenControl.context: What a paired screen that can control can do.

account.accessRules.screenKeeps.en: Keep working when you log out elsewhere
account.accessRules.screenKeeps.context: What a paired screen can do: it keeps working when the person logs out on another device.

account.accessRules.screenNoEdit.en: Edit dashboards, open other panels or your account
account.accessRules.screenNoEdit.context: What a paired screen can’t do.

account.accessRules.screenShow.en: Show the {panel} wall panel and its dashboards, live
account.accessRules.screenShow.context: What a paired screen can do.

params.panel: The wall panel’s name. Not translated.

account.accessRules.screenShowChosen.en: Show the chosen wall panel and its dashboards, live
account.accessRules.screenShowChosen.context: What a paired screen can do, before a wall panel is chosen.

account.actions.deleteFailed.en: Your account couldn’t be deleted. Nothing changed; please try again.
account.actions.deleteFailed.context: Red text in the delete dialog when deleting the account failed.

account.actions.deletionFailed.context: Title of a red message when the dialog that deletes the account couldn’t open.

account.actions.downloadFailed.context: Title of a red message when downloading everything Tiledash keeps for the person failed.

account.actions.downloadTooOften.en: You downloaded it a few times just now. Please try again later.
account.actions.downloadTooOften.context: Text under "Couldn’t download your data" when it was downloaded too often in a short time.

account.actions.extraPinAdded.context: Green message after another PIN was added on the PIN card. {name} is its name, such as "Kids".

params.name: The name of the new PIN.

account.actions.homeyRemoved.context: Message (toast) after a Homey was removed from Tiledash on Settings › Profile, with its dashboards and history.

params.homey: The name of the Homey, as the person named it. Not translated.

account.actions.pinFailed.context: Red text on the PIN card when saving or removing the PIN failed, used when no more specific reason is known.

account.actions.pinNameTaken.context: Red text on the PIN card when another of the account’s PINs already has that name.

account.actions.pinRemoved.context: Green message after the account’s PIN was removed.

account.actions.pinSaved.context: Green message after the account’s PIN was set or changed.

account.actions.pinTaken.en: That PIN is already in use. Pick other digits.
account.actions.pinTaken.context: Red text on the PIN card when the digits typed are already the account’s own PIN or one of its other PINs (each PIN must be different).

account.actions.removeHomeyFailed.context: Shown in the confirmation dialog when removing a Homey from Tiledash failed.

account.actions.removedDevice.context: Shown instead of a device’s name on Account → Recordings when the device was deleted in Homey.

account.actions.stopCancel.context: Button of the question that keeps the recording.

account.actions.stopConfirm.context: Red button of the question that stops the recording and deletes its history.

account.actions.stopFailed.context: Title of a red message when stopping a recording failed. The reason follows under it.

account.actions.stopTitle.context: Title of the question before stopping a recording (its history is deleted with it).

account.actions.stopped.context: Message (toast) after a recording was stopped.

params.device: The name of the device. Not translated.
params.reading: The name of the reading, such as "Temperature".

account.actions.tryAgain.context: Text under a red message, used when no more specific reason is known.

account.actions.tryLater.en: Please try again in a moment.
account.actions.tryLater.context: Text under a red message about downloading or deleting.

account.aiAssistants.allow0.en: Read and change your own widgets and partials, and see their history
account.aiAssistants.allow0.context: What a connected assistant can do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsAllow0.

account.aiAssistants.allow1.context: What a connected assistant can do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsAllow1.

account.aiAssistants.allow2.en: Read your devices: their names, kinds, capabilities and current readings
account.aiAssistants.allow2.context: What a connected assistant can do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsAllow2.

account.aiAssistants.allow3.en: Read the names of your themes
account.aiAssistants.allow3.context: What a connected assistant can do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsAllow3.

account.aiAssistants.allow4.en: Make and change your own furniture models for floor plans, and see their history
account.aiAssistants.allow4.context: What a connected assistant can do (F18). Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsAllow4.

account.aiAssistants.appLine.en: from {host} · connected {date} · {used, select, yes {used {lastUsed}} other {not used yet}}{links, plural, =0 {} one { · # preview link} other { · # preview links}}
account.aiAssistants.appLine.context: Line under a connected app’s name: the web address it came from, when it was connected, when it was last used, and how many preview links it has.

params.date: When it was connected, such as "3 October".
params.host: The app’s web address, such as "claude.ai". Not translated.
params.lastUsed: How long ago it was last used, such as "5 min ago".
params.links: How many preview links it has.
params.used: "yes" when it was used, "no" when not yet.

account.aiAssistants.askDisconnect.en: Disconnect {app}? Its preview links stop too.

params.app: The app’s name, such as "Claude". Not translated.

account.aiAssistants.assistant.context: Name of the row of choices of AI assistant, read out by screen readers.

account.aiAssistants.canSwitch.context: Warning on a preview link whose taps reach the Homey: until when the app can switch the device.

params.time: A time of day, such as "14:32".

account.aiAssistants.connectTitle.context: Heading of the card with the steps to connect an AI assistant.

account.aiAssistants.connected.context: Heading of the list of AI assistants (apps) connected to Tiledash.

account.aiAssistants.copied.context: Button text for a moment after copying the address or command.

account.aiAssistants.copy.context: Button that copies the address, file or command.

account.aiAssistants.deny0.en: Switch your devices or start flows (only you can let a preview’s taps through, for an hour)
account.aiAssistants.deny0.context: What a connected assistant can’t do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsDeny0.

account.aiAssistants.deny1.en: Read your history, dashboards, billing or account
account.aiAssistants.deny1.context: What a connected assistant can’t do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsDeny1.

account.aiAssistants.deny2.en: See your Homey password or tokens
account.aiAssistants.deny2.context: What a connected assistant can’t do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsDeny2.

account.aiAssistants.deny3.en: Reach anyone else’s widgets or models
account.aiAssistants.deny3.context: What a connected assistant can’t do. Use the same words as login.consent.widgetsDeny3.

account.aiAssistants.disconnect.context: Button that disconnects an app (it asks first); also the red button that does it.

account.aiAssistants.free.en: Building widgets with an assistant needs Pro. You can connect now; it starts working once you’re on Pro.
account.aiAssistants.free.context: Note on the Free plan: building widgets with an AI assistant needs Pro, the paid plan.

account.aiAssistants.keep.context: Button that keeps the app connected after all.

account.aiAssistants.lead.en: Build and polish your widgets and floor plan furniture with the AI you already use: Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot in VS Code, Cursor. Connect it once; you sign in with your Homey account, and it gets a key that only works for your widgets and models.
account.aiAssistants.lead.context: Text at the top of the AI assistants tab. Keep the product names. Floor plan furniture: 3D pieces the assistant can design for the person’s floor plans.

account.aiAssistants.none.en: No assistant connected yet. Connect one below.
account.aiAssistants.none.context: Shown when no AI assistant is connected.

account.aiAssistants.previewModel.context: A preview link of an app that shows a piece of furniture it designs for the floor plan (bold: its name). There are no taps on it.

params.model: The model’s name, such as "Reading chair". Not translated.

account.aiAssistants.previewOn.context: A preview link of an app: the widget (bold) and which device it draws.

account.aiAssistants.previewOnTest.context: A preview link of an app that draws a test or demo device: the widget (bold).

account.aiAssistants.rulesTitle.en: What a connected assistant can do
account.aiAssistants.rulesTitle.context: Heading of the lists of what a connected assistant can and can’t do.

account.aiAssistants.send.context: Switch on a preview link: taps in the preview really switch the device, for an hour.

account.aiAssistants.sendLabel.en: Send taps from {app}’s preview to my Homey
account.aiAssistants.sendLabel.context: Name of the switch, read out by screen readers.

account.aiAssistants.simulated.context: On a preview link of test data: taps never reach a real device.

account.aiAssistants.upgrade.context: Button in the note that opens paying for Pro.

account.alertRules.always.context: Choice of when a device’s alert wakes the screens: at any time.

account.alertRules.armed.context: Choice of when a device’s alert wakes the screens: only while the home alarm is armed.

account.alertRules.armedMeans.context: Label of the choice of home alarm whose state counts as "armed".

account.alertRules.cameraLabel.context: Name of the choice of camera for a device’s alert, read out by screen readers.

params.device: The name of the device. Not translated.

account.alertRules.chime.context: Label of the switch that plays a sound with alerts.

account.alertRules.chimeHint.en: Beeps for danger, ding-dong for the bell. A browser lets it sound after one tap on the screen.
account.alertRules.chimeHint.context: Hint under "Chime": what it sounds like, and that a browser only plays sound after someone tapped the screen once.

account.alertRules.chimeLabel.context: Name of the switch, read out by screen readers.

account.alertRules.danger.context: Heading of the group of devices that raise danger alerts.

account.alertRules.dangerHint.en: Smoke, CO, water and sirens. They wake the screens day and night unless you say otherwise.
account.alertRules.dangerHint.context: Line under "Danger". CO is carbon monoxide.

account.alertRules.default.context: Small hint next to the choice that is the default for this kind of device. Lower case.

account.alertRules.flowLabel.context: Name of the choice of flow, read out by screen readers.

account.alertRules.homeAlarm.context: Name of the choice of home alarm, read out by screen readers.

account.alertRules.never.context: Choice of when a device’s alert wakes the screens: never.

account.alertRules.news.context: Heading of the group of devices that raise milder alerts: the doorbell, motion, doors.

account.alertRules.newsHint.en: The doorbell always; motion and doors only while the alarm is armed, unless you say otherwise.
account.alertRules.newsHint.context: Line under "News", the group of milder alerts: which of those devices wake the screens by default.

account.alertRules.night.context: Choice of when a device’s alert wakes the screens: only during the night hours set below.

account.alertRules.nightFor.context: Hint under "Night" while no alert uses it. Use the same words as the choice "At night".

account.alertRules.nightFrom.context: Name of the choice of when the night starts, read out by screen readers.

account.alertRules.nightLabel.context: Label of the night hours, used by alerts set to "At night".

account.alertRules.nightOwnTime.context: Hint under "Night": the hours are in each wall panel’s own time zone.

account.alertRules.nightTo.context: Name of the choice of when the night ends, read out by screen readers.

account.alertRules.noAlarm.context: Choice: there is no home alarm.

account.alertRules.noAlarmHint.en: Without one, “While armed” never wakes the screens.
account.alertRules.noAlarmHint.context: Hint under "Armed means" when no home alarm is chosen. Use the same words as the choice "While armed".

account.alertRules.noCamera.context: Choice of camera: no camera comes along with this device’s alert.

account.alertRules.noRoom.context: Under a device that isn’t in any room of the house.

account.alertRules.none.context: Shown under "Danger" or "News" when the Homey has no such devices.

account.alertRules.nowArmed.context: Hint under "Armed means": the chosen home alarm is armed right now.

account.alertRules.nowNotArmed.context: Hint under "Armed means": the chosen home alarm isn’t armed right now.

account.alertRules.offerFlow.context: Label of the choice of a flow (a Homey automation) to offer as a button on danger alerts.

account.alertRules.offerFlowHint.en: A button on danger alerts, e.g. “Everyone out”.
account.alertRules.offerFlowHint.context: Hint under "Offer a flow". "Everyone out" is an example of a flow’s name.

account.alertRules.roomCameras.context: Choice of camera that comes along with a device’s alert: the cameras in the device’s own room, named.

params.cameras: The names of the cameras, already joined as a list. Not translated.

account.alertRules.roomNoCamera.context: Choice of camera: the cameras in the device’s own room, when the room has none.

account.alertRules.screensHint.en: They wake from their sleep screen and show the alert full screen. Others show a bar on top.
account.alertRules.screensHint.context: Line under "Screens that wake for alerts".

account.alertRules.screensTitle.context: Heading above the list of wall panels to tick.

account.alertRules.to.context: Word between the start and the end of the night, such as "22:00 to 07:00".

account.alertRules.whenLabel.context: Name of the choice of when a device’s alert wakes the screens, read out by screen readers.

params.device: The name of the device. Not translated.

account.billing.choose.context: Button in the "back to Free" panel that opens the choice of which recordings, dashboards or Homey keep going on Free.

account.billing.dashboardsAllStay.en: {count, plural, one {Your # dashboard stays} other {Your # dashboards stay}}
account.billing.dashboardsAllStay.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account has no more dashboards than Free allows.

account.billing.dashboardsStay.en: {limit, plural, one {# of your {total} dashboards stays} other {# of your {total} dashboards stay}}
account.billing.dashboardsStay.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account has more dashboards than Free allows: only this many stay active.

account.billing.dashboardsStayText.en: {paused, plural, one {Free has room for {limit}. Choose which; the other one is paused, kept as it is, and back with Pro.} other {Free has room for {limit}. Choose which; the other # are paused, kept as they are, and back with Pro.}}
account.billing.dashboardsStayText.context: Text under "… of your … dashboards stay": the person chooses which stay; the others are paused, not deleted, and come back with Pro.

account.billing.historyHidden.en: Older history is hidden, not deleted
account.billing.historyHidden.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel about recorded history beyond what Free keeps.

account.billing.historyHiddenText.en: Free shows {detailed, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} in detail and {hourly, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} hourly. The rest is kept for {kept, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, so it’s all back if you return to Pro.
account.billing.historyHiddenText.context: Text under "Older history is hidden, not deleted": how much history Free shows, and how long the rest is kept in case the person goes back to Pro.

params.detailed: Days of detailed history Free shows.
params.hourly: Days of hourly history Free shows.
params.kept: Days the hidden history is kept.

account.billing.homeysStay.en: {limit, plural, one {# of your {total} Homeys stays connected} other {# of your {total} Homeys stay connected}}
account.billing.homeysStay.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account has more Homeys than Free allows: only this many stay connected.

account.billing.homeysStayText.en: {paused, plural, one {Choose which; the other one is paused: its dashboards and recordings wait until you go Pro again.} other {Choose which; the other # are paused: their dashboards and recordings wait until you go Pro again.}}
account.billing.homeysStayText.context: Text under "… of your … Homeys stay connected": the person chooses which; the others pause with their dashboards and recordings.

account.billing.monthsFree.en: {count, plural, one {# month free} other {# months free}}
account.billing.monthsFree.context: What paying yearly saves against paying monthly, when it is about whole months, such as "2 months free". Shown next to "Yearly".

params.count: How many months a year of Pro saves.

account.billing.price.en: {interval, select, month {{price} a month} other {{price} a year}}
account.billing.price.context: A price of Pro with how often it is paid, such as "€4 a month" or "€40 a year".

params.price: The amount with its currency, such as "€4".

account.billing.recordingInterval.en: {minute, select, yes {At most every minute, as Free records.} other {At most every {seconds} s, as Free records.}}
account.billing.recordingInterval.context: Text under "All … recordings keep going": on Free a reading is recorded at most this often.

params.minute: "yes" when Free records at most once a minute, "no" otherwise.
params.seconds: How many seconds apart, when not a minute.

account.billing.recordingSame.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account records nothing: recording works on Free as before.

account.billing.recordingsKeepGoing.en: {count, plural, one {Your # recording keeps going} other {All # recordings keep going}}
account.billing.recordingsKeepGoing.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account records no more readings than Free allows: they all go on.

account.billing.recordingsPause.en: {over, plural, one {# recording of your {total} pauses} other {# recordings of your {total} pause}}
account.billing.recordingsPause.context: Line in the "back to Free" panel when the account records more readings than Free allows: this many of them pause.

params.total: How many recordings there are in all.

account.billing.recordingsPauseText.en: Free records {limit}. Choose which keep going; the others pause and keep their history.
account.billing.recordingsPauseText.context: Text under "… recordings of your … pause".

params.limit: How many readings Free records: a bare number, so add the noun your language needs.

account.billing.save.context: What paying yearly saves against paying monthly, such as "save 17%". Shown next to "Yearly", after a dot, so lower case.

params.percent: The saving, as a percentage such as "17%".

account.billingActions.alreadyPro.context: Title of a red message when the person subscribed to Pro while already having it (for example from a second tab).

account.billingActions.alreadyProBody.en: The new subscription was cancelled, so you don’t pay twice.

account.billingActions.cancelFailed.context: Title of a red message when cancelling the Pro subscription failed.

account.billingActions.checkConnection.en: Check your connection and try again.
account.billingActions.checkConnection.context: Text under a failed payment action when the browser got no answer at all.

account.billingActions.checkoutFailed.context: Title of a red message when paying for Pro couldn’t start.

account.billingActions.confirmFailed.context: Title of a red message when Pro couldn’t start after paying.

account.billingActions.confirmFailedBody.en: PayPal approved it, but Tiledash couldn’t check it. {advice}
account.billingActions.confirmFailedBody.context: Text under "Couldn’t start Pro" after paying with PayPal: PayPal said yes, but Tiledash couldn’t confirm the subscription.

params.advice: A sentence saying what to try, already translated.

account.billingActions.portalFailed.context: Title of a red message when the payment provider’s billing page couldn’t be opened.

account.billingActions.switchFailed.en: {interval, select, year {Couldn’t switch to yearly} other {Couldn’t switch to monthly}}
account.billingActions.switchFailed.context: Title of a red message when switching between paying monthly and yearly failed.

params.interval: "year" or "month": what it tried to switch to.

account.billingActions.tryLater.en: Please try again in a moment.
account.billingActions.tryLater.context: Text under a failed payment action for any other reason.

account.calendarToasts.added.context: Toast after a calendar (an iCal link) was added on the account page. {name} is its name.

account.calendarToasts.loadFailed.context: Shown on the account page when the list of calendars couldn’t be read.

account.calendarToasts.removeFailed.context: Toast when removing a calendar from the account failed.

account.calendarToasts.removed.context: Toast after a calendar was removed from the account. {name} is its name.

account.calendarToasts.saveFailed.context: Error in the calendar dialog when saving it failed.

account.calendarToasts.saved.context: Toast after a calendar was changed on the account page. {name} is its name.

account.calendars.add.context: Button in the Calendars card that opens the dialog to add a calendar by its iCal link.

account.calendars.cancel.context: Button in a calendar dialog that closes it without saving.

account.calendars.colour.context: Label of the colour choice of a calendar; widgets can show its events in it.

account.calendars.dialogAdd.context: Title of the dialog that adds a calendar by its iCal link.

account.calendars.dialogEdit.context: Title of the dialog that changes a calendar. {name} is its name.

account.calendars.edit.context: Button on a calendar in the Calendars card: change its name, colour or link.

account.calendars.empty.context: Shown in the Calendars card while the account has none.

account.calendars.failedNever.context: Status of a calendar whose link has never loaded, in red.

account.calendars.failedSince.context: First part of the status of a calendar whose link fails, in red. {time} is when it started failing, such as 09:40 or a date.

account.calendars.keptEvents.en: Widgets show its events as they were at {time}.
account.calendars.keptEvents.context: Small text under a failing calendar: tiles keep showing the events from the last time it loaded. {time} is that moment, formatted.

account.calendars.lead.en: Add a calendar’s private iCal link, and widgets can show its events. Tiledash keeps the link encrypted and loads it every 15 minutes.
account.calendars.lead.context: Text at the top of the Calendars card on the account page. An iCal link is a web address a calendar app (Google, iCloud, Outlook) gives to read a calendar. It is private: anyone with it can read the calendar.

account.calendars.limit.context: Small text at the foot of the Calendars card: how many calendars the account has out of what its plan allows. {plan} is the plan’s name (Free or Pro).

account.calendars.limitUpgrade.context: Link after the count of calendars on Free, leading to the upgrade. {limit} is how many calendars Pro allows.

account.calendars.link.context: Label of the field for a calendar’s web address (an iCal link, https:// or webcal://).

account.calendars.linkBad.en: Paste a link that starts with https:// or webcal://.
account.calendars.linkBad.context: Error under the link field of a calendar when what was typed is not such a web address.

account.calendars.linkKept.en: The link from {host} is kept. Paste a new one to replace it.
account.calendars.linkKept.context: Hint under the empty link field when editing a calendar: its link is a secret and isn’t shown again. {host} is the link’s site, such as calendar.google.com.

params.host: The site of the link, such as calendar.google.com.

account.calendars.loaded.en: {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} in the next 30 days · loaded at {time}
account.calendars.loaded.context: Status line of a calendar that loads fine. {events} is how many events it has in the next 30 days, {time} when it was last loaded, such as 10:12.

params.time: The time it was loaded, formatted.

account.calendars.loading.context: Status of a calendar just added, while its link is loaded for the first time.

account.calendars.name.context: Label of the field for a calendar’s name, such as “Family”.

account.calendars.namePlaceholder.context: Example name in the empty name field of a calendar.

account.calendars.paused.en: Paused: {plan} keeps {limit, plural, one {# calendar} other {# calendars}}. Widgets don’t show it.
account.calendars.paused.context: Status of a calendar past what the plan allows (after going back from Pro to Free): it isn’t loaded and widgets don’t show its events. {plan} is the plan’s name, {limit} how many calendars it keeps.

params.limit: How many calendars the plan keeps.
params.plan: The plan’s name, Free or Pro.

account.calendars.pickAll.context: First choice of a widget’s calendar setting: show the events of every calendar of the account, also ones added later.

account.calendars.pickFailing.context: Small red note after a calendar’s name in a widget’s calendar setting, when its link fails. Lower case.

account.calendars.pickNone.en: No calendars yet. Add one under Settings › Calendars.
account.calendars.pickNone.context: Shown in a widget’s calendar setting while the account has no calendars.

account.calendars.problemNotCalendar.en: The link doesn’t lead to a calendar. Use the link that ends in .ics.
account.calendars.problemNotCalendar.context: Why a calendar can’t be loaded: the web address gives something else than an iCal calendar, such as a web page.

account.calendars.problemNotFound.en: The link isn’t there anymore. Was the calendar unshared, or its link reset?
account.calendars.problemNotFound.context: Why a calendar can’t be loaded: its web address answers “not found”. Calendar apps let people reset a private link, which ends the old one.

account.calendars.problemRefused.en: The calendar’s server refused. The link may need signing in; use the private iCal link.
account.calendars.problemRefused.context: Why a calendar can’t be loaded: its server refused (it asked to sign in, or forbade it). The private iCal link works without signing in.

account.calendars.problemTooBig.en: The calendar is over 5 MB, too big to load.
account.calendars.problemTooBig.context: Why a calendar can’t be loaded: the file it gives is larger than 5 megabytes.

account.calendars.problemUnreachable.en: The calendar’s server didn’t answer. Tiledash keeps trying.
account.calendars.problemUnreachable.context: Why a calendar can’t be loaded: its server could not be reached or took too long. It is tried again every 15 minutes.

account.calendars.remove.context: Button on a calendar in the Calendars card: remove it from the account.

account.calendars.removeText.en: Widgets showing it lose its events. Its link is deleted from Tiledash.
account.calendars.removeText.context: Text of the dialog that asks before removing a calendar.

account.calendars.removeTitle.context: Title of the dialog that asks before removing a calendar. {name} is its name.

account.calendars.retry.context: Button on a calendar whose link failed to load: load it again now.

account.calendars.save.context: Button in the calendar dialog that saves it.

account.calendars.title.context: Heading of the card on the account page that lists the calendars (iCal links) added to the account.

account.calendars.whereApple.en: iCloud: Calendar › Share › Public calendar, then copy the link.
account.calendars.whereApple.context: Where Apple’s iCloud Calendar shows a calendar’s link. Use the names iCloud shows in your language.

account.calendars.whereGoogle.en: Google Calendar: Settings › your calendar › Secret address in iCal format.
account.calendars.whereGoogle.context: Where Google Calendar shows a calendar’s private link. Use the names Google Calendar shows in your language.

account.calendars.whereOutlook.en: Outlook: Settings › Calendar › Shared calendars › Publish, the ICS link.
account.calendars.whereOutlook.context: Where Outlook shows a calendar’s published link. Use the names Outlook shows in your language.

account.calendars.whereTitle.context: Small heading in the dialog that adds a calendar, over where each calendar app shows its private link.

account.configBackup.busy.en: Another import is running, or there were many tries in the last hour. Please try again later.
account.configBackup.busy.context: Text under "Couldn’t read the file" when restoring was tried too often.

account.configBackup.downloadFailed.context: Title of a red message when downloading a backup failed.

account.configBackup.downloadTooOften.en: You downloaded one a few times just now (5 an hour). Please try again later.
account.configBackup.downloadTooOften.context: Text under "Couldn’t download a backup" when it was downloaded too often.

account.configBackup.noRoom.en: Your plan doesn’t have room for everything chosen. Nothing was changed.
account.configBackup.noRoom.context: Red text in the restore dialog when the plan doesn’t allow all that was chosen.

account.configBackup.readFailed.context: Title of a red message when the chosen backup file couldn’t be read.

account.configBackup.restoreFailed.en: The restore didn’t finish. Nothing was changed. Please try again.
account.configBackup.restoreFailed.context: Red text in the restore dialog when restoring failed.

account.configBackup.tryLater.en: Please try again in a moment.
account.configBackup.tryLater.context: Text under a red message about a backup, used when no more specific reason is known.

account.configBackup.unreachable.en: Tiledash couldn’t be reached. Nothing was changed.
account.configBackup.unreachable.context: Red text in the restore dialog when the browser got no answer.

account.configBackup.yourHomey.context: Stands in for a Homey’s name in "Connect … first" and "Still reading …" when the name isn’t known. Lower case.

account.configImport.alreadyHereDetail.en: What you have here is kept as it is.

account.configImport.alreadyHereTitle.context: Heading of parts that are already set up on this account.

account.configImport.childTilesDetail.en: The widget has no Tiles setting of that name here, so these stay behind.
account.configImport.childTilesDetail.context: Line under "Tiles inside widgets without a place for them". "Tiles" is the name of a widget setting.

account.configImport.childTilesTitle.en: Tiles inside widgets without a place for them
account.configImport.childTilesTitle.context: Heading of tiles that were inside a widget, which has no place for them here.

account.configImport.connectDetail.en: This backup is for {homey}, which isn’t connected to this account. Connect it, then choose the file again.

account.configImport.connectTitle.context: Heading when the backup is for a Homey this account doesn’t have.

account.configImport.damagedDetail.en: It may not have downloaded completely. Choose another backup.
account.configImport.damagedDetail.context: Line under "This file can’t be read".

account.configImport.damagedTitle.context: Heading when the chosen file is damaged.

account.configImport.emptiedDetail.en: The tile comes along and asks for it again.
account.configImport.emptiedDetail.context: Line under "Settings naming something this Homey doesn’t have".

account.configImport.emptiedTitle.en: Settings naming something this Homey doesn’t have
account.configImport.emptiedTitle.context: Heading of tile settings that point at a device, flow or mood this Homey doesn’t have.

account.configImport.group.en: {key, select, themes {{count, plural, one {# theme} other {# themes}}} presets {{count, plural, one {# style preset} other {# style presets}}} widgets {{count, plural, one {# widget or partial} other {# widgets and partials}}} pictures {{count, plural, one {# picture} other {# pictures}}} testDevices {{count, plural, one {# test device} other {# test devices}}} floorPlans {{count, plural, one {# floor plan} other {# floor plans}}} houses {{count, plural, one {# house} other {# houses}}} other {{count, plural, one {# recording} other {# recordings}}}}
account.configImport.group.context: A part of the backup that can come along, with how many, such as "3 themes". Style presets are saved looks for tiles; partials are pieces of widget code; test devices are made-up devices for building widgets; floor plans are drawings of the house, level by level; houses are pictures of the home with places marked on them, for the Energy house tile; recordings keep a reading’s history.

params.key: Which part: themes, presets, widgets, pictures, testDevices, floorPlans, houses or recordings.

account.configImport.groupName.en: {key, select, alerts {Alert rules} energy {Energy settings} other {Account settings}}
account.configImport.groupName.context: A part of the backup that is one thing: the alert rules, the energy settings or the account settings.

params.key: Which part: alerts, energy or settings.

account.configImport.homeyMissingDetail.en: Its dashboards, wall panels and energy settings stay behind. Connect it and restore again.
account.configImport.homeyMissingDetail.context: Line under "A Homey that isn’t connected here".

account.configImport.homeyMissingTitle.en: A Homey that isn’t connected here
account.configImport.homeyMissingTitle.context: Heading of a part of the backup that stays behind: it belongs to a Homey this account doesn’t have.

account.configImport.limit.en: {key, select, dashboards {Your plan has room for {room} dashboards; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} recordings {Your plan has room for {room} recordings; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} themes {Your plan has room for {room} themes of your own; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} widgets {Your plan has room for {room} widgets of your own; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} floorPlans {Your plan has room for {room} floor plans; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} houses {Your plan has room for {room} houses; you have {have} and chose {adding}.} other {Your plan has room for {room} pictures; you have {have} and chose {adding}.}}
account.configImport.limit.context: Why the chosen parts don’t fit the plan: how many it allows, how many there are, and how many were chosen to come along.

params.adding: How many were chosen from the backup.
params.key: Which limit: dashboards, recordings, themes, widgets, floorPlans, houses or pictures.

account.configImport.missingDeviceDetail.context: Line under "Tiles whose device isn’t on this Homey".

account.configImport.missingDeviceTitle.en: Tiles whose device isn’t on this Homey
account.configImport.missingDeviceTitle.context: Heading of tiles that stay behind: the device they show isn’t on this Homey.

account.configImport.namesMore.context: The first two of several dashboard names and how many more, such as "Home, Energy and 2 more".

account.configImport.needsProDetail.en: Your own themes, widgets, partials and test devices need Pro here.

account.configImport.needsProTitle.context: Heading of parts that need Pro, the paid plan.

account.configImport.notConfigDetail.en: Choose a file made with Download a backup (Settings › Profile). Download your data gives a different zip, which can’t be restored.
account.configImport.notConfigDetail.context: Line under "This isn’t a Tiledash backup". "Download a backup", "Settings › Profile" and "Download your data" name buttons and places of the Settings page: use the same words as they do.

account.configImport.notConfigTitle.context: Heading when the chosen file isn’t a backup made by Tiledash.

account.configImport.partialKeptDetail.en: Yours are kept; the widgets that render them use yours.
account.configImport.partialKeptDetail.context: Line under "Partials you already have with another template".

account.configImport.partialKeptTitle.en: Partials you already have with another template
account.configImport.partialKeptTitle.context: Heading of partials (pieces of widget code) that exist here already with other code.

account.configImport.restore.context: Button that restores the chosen parts, when no dashboard is chosen.

account.configImport.restoreDashboards.context: Button that restores the chosen dashboards.

account.configImport.restoreDashboardsMo.en: {count, plural, one {Restore # dashboard and more} other {Restore # dashboards and more}}
account.configImport.restoreDashboardsMo.context: Button that restores the chosen dashboards and other parts (wall panels, themes…).

account.configImport.storeDetail.en: Install them here from the community; a theme falls back to the default meanwhile.

account.configImport.storeTitle.context: Heading of themes and widgets that came from the community; they aren’t in the backup.

account.configImport.syncingDetail.en: Tiledash is reading {homey}’s devices, flows and moods, so it can match the tiles to them. This takes a minute.
account.configImport.syncingDetail.context: Line under "Still reading …". Flows and moods are Homey’s automations and scenes.

account.configImport.syncingTitle.context: Heading while Tiledash is still reading the Homey’s devices, before it can restore.

account.configImport.tooLargeDetail.en: A backup is at most 64 MB. Check that you chose the right file.
account.configImport.tooLargeDetail.context: Line under "This file is too large".

account.configImport.tooLargeTitle.context: Heading when the chosen file is bigger than a backup can be.

account.configImport.tooNewDetail.en: This backup comes from a newer version of Tiledash, so it can’t be restored here.
account.configImport.tooNewDetail.context: Line under "Made by a newer Tiledash".

account.configImport.tooNewTitle.context: Heading when the backup comes from a newer version of Tiledash.

account.creditActions.added.en: {count, plural, one {# credit added} other {# credits added}}
account.creditActions.added.context: Title of a green message after buying a pack of house credits: this many were added.

params.count: How many credits the pack held.

account.creditActions.addedBody.en: You now have {balance, plural, one {# credit} other {# credits}}.
account.creditActions.addedBody.context: Text under the green message about added credits: the new balance.

params.balance: How many credits the person has now.

account.creditActions.captureFailed.en: We couldn’t add your credits yet
account.creditActions.captureFailed.context: Title of a red message when a credit purchase was approved at PayPal but Tiledash could not confirm it just now.

account.creditActions.captureFailedBody.en: If PayPal took the payment, the credits show up here as soon as it confirms it.
account.creditActions.captureFailedBody.context: Text under the red message that credits couldn’t be added yet.

account.creditActions.checkConnection.en: Check your connection and try again.
account.creditActions.checkConnection.context: Text under a failed credit purchase message when the browser got no answer at all.

account.creditActions.declined.context: Title of a message when PayPal declined the card or account a credit pack was paid with; PayPal then lets the person try another.

account.creditActions.declinedBody.en: Nothing was charged. Pick another card or pay with PayPal.
account.creditActions.declinedBody.context: Text under the message that the card was declined.

account.creditActions.notPaid.context: Title of a red message when the person approved a credit purchase at PayPal but the payment did not go through.

account.creditActions.notPaidBody.en: No credits were added, and you weren’t charged for them. Try again, or pay another way at PayPal.
account.creditActions.notPaidBody.context: Text under the red message that PayPal didn’t complete a credit payment.

account.creditActions.startFailed.context: Title of a red message when buying a credit pack couldn’t begin; nothing was charged.

account.creditActions.tryLater.en: Please try again in a moment.
account.creditActions.tryLater.context: Text under a failed credit purchase message for any other reason.

account.creditActions.unavailable.context: Text under a red message when this Tiledash install can’t take payments for credits at all.

account.credits.copyright.context: A link to OpenStreetMap’s copyright page.

account.credits.maps.context: Name of what a data source is used for: the maps.

account.credits.mapsText.en: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. Map tiles come from OpenFreeMap with OpenMapTiles unless you picked another one under Settings › General.
account.credits.mapsText.context: The credit for the maps. Map tiles are the pictures the map is drawn from; "Settings › General" names the Settings page and its group where the maps' tiles are chosen, so write them as the app names them.

account.credits.places.context: Name of what a data source is used for: searching places (addresses, towns).

account.credits.placesText.en: Places are searched with OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, under the Open Database Licence.
account.credits.placesText.context: The credit OpenStreetMap’s licence asks for.

account.credits.weather.context: Name of what a data source is used for: the weather.

account.credits.weatherText.en: Weather data from MET Norway (Locationforecast and Sunrise), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.
account.credits.weatherText.context: The credit MET Norway’s licence asks for. Locationforecast and Sunrise are the names of its services; keep them.

account.delete.confirm.context: Red button that deletes the account.

account.delete.copyBody.en: Your dashboards, settings and themes as JSON, your history as CSV, in one zip.
account.delete.copyBody.context: Text after "Want a copy first?". JSON and CSV are file formats; zip is a compressed file.

account.delete.copyTitle.context: Bold question in the delete dialog, before the download button.

account.delete.dashboards.context: Item of the list of what is deleted.

account.delete.download.context: Button in the delete dialog that downloads everything Tiledash keeps for the person.

account.delete.goesLabel.context: Name of the list of what is deleted, read out by screen readers.

account.delete.homeyLink.en: {count, plural, one {The link to your Homey} other {The link to your # Homeys}}
account.delete.homeyLink.context: Last item of the list of what is deleted: Tiledash’s connection to the person’s Homeys.

account.delete.keep.context: Button that closes the delete dialog without deleting.

account.delete.lead.en: This removes everything you made in Tiledash. Your Homey itself isn’t touched: its devices, flows and Insights stay as they are.
account.delete.lead.context: Text at the top of the delete dialog. Insights is Homey’s own history; keep the name.

account.delete.proNoRefund.en: It isn’t refunded for the rest of the period (until {date}).
account.delete.proNoRefund.context: Text of the warning: the rest of the paid period isn’t paid back.

account.delete.proStops.context: Title of a warning in the delete dialog when the person pays for Pro.

account.delete.recordings.en: {count, plural, one {# recording and all the history it kept} other {# recordings and all the history they kept}}
account.delete.recordings.context: Item of the list of what is deleted: recorded readings and their history.

account.delete.themes.en: {count, plural, one {# theme of your own} other {# themes of your own}}
account.delete.themes.context: Item of the list of what is deleted: the themes the person made.

account.delete.title.context: Title of the dialog that deletes the Tiledash account.

account.delete.typeLabel.context: Name of the field where the person types the word, read out by screen readers.

params.word: The word to type, such as "delete".

account.delete.typeToConfirm.context: Label above the field where the person types the word. The word is bold.

params.word: The word to type, such as "delete".

account.delete.wallPanels.en: {count, plural, one {# wall panel} other {# wall panels}}
account.delete.wallPanels.context: Item of the list of what is deleted. A wall panel is a screen on the wall paired with Tiledash.

account.delete.when.en: You’re signed out everywhere and your wall panels stop straight away. On {date} it’s gone for good; log in before then to keep your account.
account.delete.when.context: Line in the delete dialog: what happens at once, and when the account is deleted for good. The date is bold.

account.delete.word.context: The word the person types to confirm deleting the account. One short lower-case word, easy to type; English "delete" also works.

account.discord.bugs.context: Title of a link to the channel on Tiledash’s Discord server where people report bugs.

account.discord.bugsAbout.en: Something not working? Tell us what you did and what went wrong.
account.discord.bugsAbout.context: Line under "Bug reports" in the Discord settings group.

account.discord.chat.context: Title of a link to the general chat channel on Tiledash’s Discord server, where people talk about Tiledash and their dashboards.

account.discord.chatAbout.en: Talk with other Tiledash users, share your dashboards and ask how they did theirs.
account.discord.chatAbout.context: Line under "General chat" in the Discord settings group.

account.discord.ideas.context: Title of a link to the channel on Tiledash’s Discord server where people ask for new features.

account.discord.ideasAbout.en: Missing something? Tell us what you’d like Tiledash to do next.
account.discord.ideasAbout.context: Line under "Feature requests" in the Discord settings group.

account.discord.opens.en: Opens Discord in a new tab
account.discord.opens.context: Read out by screen readers after each link of the Discord settings group: the link opens Discord in a new browser tab.

account.extraPins.add.context: Button that opens the form to add another PIN with a name.

account.extraPins.lead.en: Give someone a PIN of their own, such as the kids for the front door. Each action that asks for a PIN says which ones it takes; yours always works.
account.extraPins.lead.context: Text under the "Other PINs" heading. An action is something a device does that asks for a PIN first, such as unlocking a door.

account.extraPins.name.context: Label of the field for the name of another PIN, such as "Kids" or "Cleaner".

account.extraPins.namePlaceholder.context: Example name in the empty name field of another PIN.

account.extraPins.nameTaken.context: Error under the name of a new PIN when another PIN has the same name.

account.extraPins.none.context: Shown in the "Other PINs" list while there are none.

account.extraPins.overviewNone.en: Nothing asks for a PIN yet. Pick actions in a device’s details.
account.extraPins.overviewNone.context: Shown under "What asks for a PIN" while no action asks for one.

account.extraPins.overviewOpen.context: Spoken name (screen readers) of the button on a device in the list of what asks for a PIN; it opens that device’s details, where its actions are chosen. {device} is the device’s name.

account.extraPins.overviewTitle.context: Small heading on the PIN card of the account page, over a list of every device action that asks for a PIN (such as Front door · Unlock) with the names of the PINs it takes. The PINs themselves are never shown.

account.extraPins.overviewYours.context: Name shown for the account’s own PIN in the list of what asks for a PIN.

account.extraPins.removeBody.en: Actions that took it then ask for your own PIN only.
account.extraPins.removeBody.context: Text after "Remove {name}?" explaining what happens when another PIN is removed.

account.extraPins.removeTitle.context: Bold start of the question before removing another PIN. {name} is its name.

params.name: The PIN’s name, such as Kids.

account.extraPins.title.context: Small heading on the PIN card of the account page, over a list of extra PINs with a name each (such as "Kids"), besides the account’s own PIN.

account.extraPins.usedBy.en: {count, plural, =0 {Asked for by nothing yet} one {Asked for by # action} other {Asked for by # actions}}
account.extraPins.usedBy.context: Small text under the name of another PIN: how many protected actions take it. {count} is that number.

params.count: How many actions take this PIN.

account.houseCredits.balance.context: Spoken label of the big number that shows how many house credits the person has left, such as "8 credits".

params.count: How many credits the person has.

account.houseCredits.buy.context: Button that opens the choice of a credit pack to buy, on the house credits card.

account.houseCredits.buyBody.en: One credit makes one picture of one side, with its spots placed. A try that fails gives its credit back. Credits don’t expire.
account.houseCredits.buyBody.context: Explains what a house credit buys, in the area where the person picks a pack. A side is one side of a house (front, back, garden). Spots are the places on the picture where things like lamps and doors are marked.

account.houseCredits.buyTitle.context: Heading of the area where the person picks a credit pack and pays for it.

account.houseCredits.givenBack.context: Line in the credit history when Tiledash’s team gave a credit back for a bad picture, without a reason.

account.houseCredits.givenBackWhy.context: Line in the credit history when Tiledash’s team gave a credit back for a bad picture, with the reason they wrote.

params.reason: The reason, written by Tiledash’s team in English, such as "two front doors".

account.houseCredits.granted.context: Line in the credit history when Tiledash’s team gave credits as a gift or for support, without a reason.

account.houseCredits.grantedWhy.context: Line in the credit history when Tiledash’s team gave credits as a gift or for support, with the reason they wrote.

params.reason: The reason, written by Tiledash’s team in English, such as "for the bug".

account.houseCredits.historyLabel.context: Spoken label of the list of changes to the person’s house credits.

account.houseCredits.intro.en: For making pictures of your houses.
account.houseCredits.intro.context: Line under the title of the house credits card.

account.houseCredits.noHistory.en: No credits bought yet. They appear here when you do.
account.houseCredits.noHistory.context: Shown in place of the history on the house credits card when nothing has changed the balance yet.

account.houseCredits.notNow.context: Button that closes the choice of a credit pack to buy without buying.

account.houseCredits.outTitle.context: Heading of the area where the person buys a credit pack, shown when they have no credits left.

account.houseCredits.pack10.en: A house, front and back, with a few tries
account.houseCredits.pack10.context: Hint under the small credit pack (10 credits) saying what it is good for. A try is one generated picture.

account.houseCredits.pack25.en: A few houses, or every style
account.houseCredits.pack25.context: Hint under the larger credit pack (25 credits) saying what it is good for. A style is a look the generated picture can have.

account.houseCredits.packCredits.context: How many credits a pack holds, on the pack’s button, such as "10 credits".

params.count: How many credits the pack holds.

account.houseCredits.packsLabel.context: Spoken label of the choice between credit packs (a radio group); a pack is a set of credits sold together.

account.houseCredits.purchase.en: Bought {count, plural, one {# credit} other {# credits}} · PayPal
account.houseCredits.purchase.context: Line in the credit history for a purchase of a pack, paid with PayPal, such as "Bought 10 credits · PayPal".

account.houseCredits.refund.context: Line in the credit history when a payment was refunded and the unspent credits of that pack were taken back.

account.houseCredits.returned.context: Line in the credit history when making a picture failed, so the credit was returned automatically.

account.houseCredits.spend.context: Line in the credit history for a credit spent on making a picture of a house.

account.houseCredits.title.context: Title of the card on the account’s Plan page that shows how many credits the person has for making pictures of their houses.

account.houseCredits.today.context: When a credit change happened, on the day itself, such as "Today, 14:20".

params.time: A time of day, such as "14:20".

account.houseCredits.unavailable.context: Shown on the house credits card instead of the buy button when this Tiledash install can’t take payments.

account.houseCredits.vat.en: Prices include VAT. You get a receipt by email.
account.houseCredits.vat.context: Small print under the credit packs. The receipt comes from the payment provider.

account.houseCredits.withPro.context: Line in the credit history: the credits that come with Pro, given once, the first time the person paid for Pro.

account.houseCredits.yesterday.context: When a credit change happened, the day before, such as "Yesterday, 14:20".

params.time: A time of day, such as "14:20".

account.importDialog.adds.en: Adds to what you have; nothing here changes.
account.importDialog.adds.context: Short line next to the buttons: restoring only adds.

account.importDialog.all.context: Checkbox that ticks or unticks every dashboard.

account.importDialog.also.context: Line after restoring: what else was made (themes, widgets…).

params.made: What else was made, already joined.

account.importDialog.alsoBring.context: Heading of the other parts of the backup to choose from: themes, widgets, settings…

account.importDialog.anotherFile.context: Button that goes back to choosing another file.

account.importDialog.cancel.context: Button that closes the dialog or stops reading the file.

account.importDialog.cantCome.context: Heading of the list of what stays behind, and why.

account.importDialog.checkAgain.context: Button that asks again whether the Homey has been read.

account.importDialog.chooseAnother.context: Button that goes back to choosing a file.

account.importDialog.chooseFile.context: Button that opens the file picker.

account.importDialog.connectHomey.context: Button that opens connecting another Homey to this account.

account.importDialog.dashboards.context: Heading of the backup’s dashboards to choose from.

account.importDialog.done.context: Button that closes the dialog after restoring.

account.importDialog.drop.context: Bold line in the area where a file can be dropped (dragged onto it).

account.importDialog.exported.context: Line about the chosen backup: its file name (bold) and when it was made.

params.date: A date and time, such as "12 October 2026, 14:05".

account.importDialog.failedBody.en: Nothing was restored and nothing here changed. Try again, or choose another backup.
account.importDialog.failedBody.context: Text under the reason when restoring failed.

account.importDialog.homeyConnected.context: Green badge: a Homey the backup is for, which is connected to this account.

account.importDialog.homeyNotConnected.context: Yellow badge: a Homey the backup is for, which isn’t connected to this account.

account.importDialog.homeyNotHere.context: Badge on a dashboard whose Homey isn’t connected here, so it can’t come along.

account.importDialog.issue.context: One kind of thing that stayed behind: its heading (bold) and its line.

account.importDialog.lead.en: Brings back dashboards, wall panels, themes and widgets from a backup. What you choose is added next to what you have; nothing you have now changes.
account.importDialog.lead.context: Text at the top of the dialog, before a file is chosen.

account.importDialog.matching.en: Matching its tiles to your Homey’s devices.

account.importDialog.neededBy.context: Under a part that a chosen dashboard needs, so it comes along anyway.

params.dashboards: The dashboards’ names, already joined as a list.

account.importDialog.needsPro.context: Under a part that needs Pro, the paid plan, on this account.

account.importDialog.noHistory.en: A backup holds no recorded history: recordings start again from the moment you restore.
account.importDialog.noHistory.context: Note at the bottom of the first step.

account.importDialog.open.context: Button that opens a restored dashboard.

account.importDialog.orChoose.context: Line under "Drop the backup here": or click to choose it. "tiledash-backup-….zip" is the name a backup file has; keep it as it is.

account.importDialog.overBody.context: Text of the red banner: why it doesn’t fit, then what to do.

params.limit: A whole sentence about the limit, already translated.

account.importDialog.overFooter.en: More than your plan has room for: untick some.
account.importDialog.overFooter.context: Short line next to the buttons when the chosen parts don’t fit the plan.

account.importDialog.overTitle.en: More than your plan has room for
account.importDialog.overTitle.context: Title of a red banner when the chosen parts don’t fit the plan.

account.importDialog.reading.context: Shown while the chosen file is being read.

account.importDialog.ready.en: {count, plural, one {# dashboard is ready. Recordings start again from now.} other {# dashboards are ready. Recordings start again from now.}}
account.importDialog.ready.context: Line after restoring: how many dashboards came back.

account.importDialog.seePro.context: Button that opens the plans, under parts that need Pro.

account.importDialog.stayedBehind.context: Heading of the folded list of what didn’t come along after restoring.

account.importDialog.step1.en: A backup comes from Account › Profile → Download a backup.
account.importDialog.step1.context: First step: where a backup is made. The bold parts name a page, its tab and a button: use the same words as the app does (shell.names.account, shell.names.profile, account.profile.downloadBackup).

account.importDialog.step2.en: Connect the same Homey here first.
account.importDialog.step2.context: Second step, when no Homey is connected yet.

account.importDialog.step2Connected.en: Connect the same Homey here. {homey} is connected
account.importDialog.step2Connected.context: Second step, when a Homey is connected: its name is bold, followed by a tick.

account.importDialog.step3.en: Choose the file, see what comes back, and restore.
account.importDialog.step3.context: Third step of restoring a backup, after making one and connecting the Homey.

account.importDialog.tiles.context: How many tiles a dashboard of the backup has.

account.importDialog.tilesStay.en: {count, plural, one {# tile stays behind} other {# tiles stay behind}}
account.importDialog.tilesStay.context: Badge on a dashboard some of whose tiles can’t come along.

account.importDialog.title.context: Title of the dialog that restores a backup.

account.importDialog.titleBlocked.context: Title of the dialog when the chosen file can’t be restored.

account.importDialog.titleDone.context: Title of the dialog after the backup was restored.

account.importDialog.tryAgain.context: Button that tries restoring again after it failed.

account.importDialog.wallPanels.context: Heading of the backup’s wall panels to choose from.

account.keepChoices.lastMonth.context: Under a dashboard that was last opened 30 to 59 days ago.

account.keepChoices.lastWeek.context: Under a dashboard that was last opened 7 to 13 days ago.

account.keepChoices.monthsAgo.context: Under a dashboard that was last opened 2 or more months ago.
